Files: avrl/exp/e03_bootstrap_sig.py, avrl/runs/E03/result.json.

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| point estimate hits, static / ts_online (of 309 corrupted groups in sim pop) | 264 / 207.9 |
| threshold_corrupted_admitted_rate / learned_corrupted_admitted_rate | 14.6% / 32.7% |

| bootstrap mean / sd | -0.172 / 0.028 |

Verdict: kill (for claim 2, at this budget, under E03's policy mapping). Script's own verdict label: KILL_REVERSED (CI excludes zero and is entirely negative), pass=false. This is not the pre-registered "kill by noise" case (CI including zero) -- it is a significant result in the direction opposite to what claim 2 requires: static/threshold admits fewer corrupted-reward groups than ts_online/learned, with high confidence. Cross-checked the point estimate against runs/p0/analyze.log's cell100/cheap 25%-budget row by reading sim_alloc.py's actual print() column order in source (not just the markdown header, which is easy to misalign against): uniform=76, static=264, static_matched=212, ts_flat=83, greedy_online=253, ts_online=208, ts_static=232, neighbor=117, oracle=309. E03's hits_static=264 and hits_ts_online=207.9 match exactly, confirming this is a real, reproducible reading and not a bootstrap-code artifact. Caveat (flagged in the plan and repeated in result.json's own note): "static" gets a free labeled quarter of cell100 clusters beyond the 25% audit budget that "ts_online" never gets, so this is not a budget-matched comparison -- it structurally favors static. sim_generic.py's existing "static_matched" policy (budget-matched, no free labels) was available and not used here, per the plan's literal static/ts_online mapping.

What it changes: combined with E01's clean double kill of claim 3 (embeddings add ~0 AUC, confident-subset proxy error 1.1% under the 3% bar, neighbor ratio 1.16x under 1.5x), claim 2 is now also unsupported on this exact config: the "learned" allocator (Thompson-sampling, online-refit) does not beat a fixed threshold at the budget phase-1 intends to spend, it loses, significantly. Only claim 1 (same policy quality, fewer expensive calls than full verification) remains untested, and is the weakest of the three claims since a naive fixed rule likely also satisfies it. This argues against funding E15's hannah GRPO run on current evidence, pending the budget-matched re-check below (the free-label asymmetry means this result is not yet the last word on claim 2).

Follow-ups:
1. (L3a, ~15 min, CPU) Rerun the identical E03 bootstrap swapping "static" for sim_generic.py's existing "static_matched" policy (budget-matched, no free labels) as the threshold analog, keeping "ts_online" as learned. Directly tests whether E03's reversal is caused by static's free-label advantage or is a real effect. Cheapest, most decision-relevant next check: static_matched already exists in the harness, no new allocator class needed (unlike G01's recalibrated threshold, which requires building one).
2. (L3b, ~15 min, CPU) Rerun E03's bootstrap at budget_frac=0.10 and 0.50 (E02's budget grid) to see if the threshold-beats-learned reversal is budget-dependent. E01's analyze.log point estimates hint the gap widens at 10% (165 static vs 95 ts_online) and narrows at 50% (299 vs 288), so a budget regime might exist where learned stops losing.
3. (L3c, larger effort, needs scoping) Rerun the same bootstrap significance test using allocators.py's actual LearnedAllocator and a literal fixed-threshold class (not sim_generic.py's static/ts_online structural analogs) against feats.parquet offline, to check whether the real phase-1 code reproduces E03's reversal or whether the analogy chosen here was misleading.

| quantity | E03 (static, free-labeled) | L3a (static_matched, budget-matched) |
|---|---|---|
| point estimate hits, threshold-analog / ts_online (of 309 corrupted groups) | 264 / 207.9 | 212.0 / 207.9 |
| threshold-analog_corrupted_admitted_rate / learned_corrupted_admitted_rate | 14.6% / 32.7% | 31.4% / 32.7% |
| point diff (threshold-analog minus learned) | -0.182 | -0.0133 |
| bootstrap 95% CI on diff (500 resamples) | [-0.225, -0.114] | [-0.0568, 0.0348] |
| bootstrap mean / sd | -0.172 / 0.028 | -0.0102 / 0.0242 |
| script's own verdict label | KILL_REVERSED | KILL |

Verdict against L3a's pre-registered thresholds: kill. Pass required the CI to exclude zero and be positive (static_matched significantly beats ts_online once budget-matched, supporting claim 2 and explaining away E03's reversal as a confound). Kill required either the CI excluding zero and negative (reversal survives budget-matching, it is real) or the CI including zero (no significant difference at this budget once matched). The observed CI [-0.0568, 0.0348] includes zero, so this is the second kill case: not distinguishable from resampling noise. Numbers were cross-checked directly from avrl/runs/L3a/result.json (not just the run report): rates recompute exactly from (309 - hits)/309 for both arms, and the e03 vs e03b script diff confirms only the static branch changed.

What it changes: E03's free-label confound is confirmed as (at least partly) responsible for the earlier reversal. Once the threshold analog is budget-matched, its point-estimate advantage over ts_online collapses from -0.182 to -0.0133, and the bootstrap CI no longer excludes zero. So the strong claim "learned loses to threshold" (E03's literal result) does not survive budget-matching. But this does not rescue claim 2 either: the pass condition (learned significantly beats a fair threshold) was also not met. At 25% budget on cell100/GSM8K/majority-vote, static_matched and ts_online are statistically indistinguishable. Combined with E01's clean kill of claim 3, the evidence for claim 2 is now "no significant edge in either direction" rather than "learned loses" -- still insufficient to justify funding E15's hannah GRPO run on current evidence, since claim 2 as stated in PROJECT.md requires that learned beats a fair threshold, not merely ties it.

Follow-ups:
1. (L4a, ~30 min total, CPU) Rerun L3a's exact script (e03b_bootstrap_matched.py, static_matched vs ts_online) at budget_frac=0.10 and 0.50, the same grid E01/E03's follow-up L3b proposed but using the validated budget-matched baseline instead of the free-label "static" L3b still plans to use. Tests whether the 25%-budget null is budget-dependent, and supersedes L3b's baseline choice now that static's free-label advantage is a known confound.
2. (L4b, ~15 min, CPU) Rerun L3a with the per-resample policy seed count raised from 8 to 32 (only SEEDS changed, everything else byte-identical) to shrink Monte Carlo noise inside each bootstrap resample. Distinguishes "genuinely tied at this budget" from "underpowered to detect a small true effect" -- the current CI is about 0.09 wide against a point diff of -0.013, so a chunk of that width could be seed noise rather than group-resampling noise.
3. (L4c, ~20 min, CPU) Rerun L3a's script with --group cell30 and --group cell300 (both columns already exist in feats.parquet, confirmed by reading it directly) instead of cell100. Tests whether the null result is sensitive to the audit-group granularity, since phase-1's actual grouping choice is not guaranteed to match cell100 and a coarser or finer grouping changes both the per-bucket budget and the classifier's fitting power.

hypothesis: a small LLM judge's error pattern (which rollouts it mis-scores, given only the question and the extracted final answer, no gold) is structured in prompt-embedding space similarly to majority-vote's error pattern (E01), but the two proxies are wrong on different, only partially overlapping subsets of prompts.
result_body:
Hypothesis: a small LLM judge's error pattern (which rollouts it mis-scores, given only the question and the extracted final answer, no gold) is structured in prompt-embedding space similarly to majority-vote's error pattern (E01), but the two proxies are wrong on different, only partially overlapping subsets of prompts.

Run: judge model Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (vLLM, temperature 0, max_tokens 6, gpu_memory_utilization 0.85), no new policy generation, reuses E01's Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct rollouts on GSM8K (avrl/runs/p0/rollouts.parquet, groups.parquet, feats.parquet: 3,000 prompts x 8 rollouts). Judge scored the 10,168 unique (pid, extracted-answer) pairs (deduplicated from 24,000 rollouts), prompted with question + proposed answer only, yes/no. Per group, judge_pick = distinct answer with the highest judge "yes"-weighted self-consistency count, ties broken toward higher count then answer string; groups where the judge said "no" to everything fall back to the group's own majority answer by construction (judge_all_no_frac = 0.0, never triggered). Scripts: avrl/exp/e04_judge_score.py, avrl/exp/e04_structure.py (both new, do not edit p0 scripts). Files: avrl/runs/E04/judge_scores.parquet, judge.log, result.json.

One real bug hit and fixed before this ran: the script's initial `gpu_memory_utilization=0.5` left vLLM's v0.19 CUDA-graph memory profiler with negative KV-cache headroom (`ValueError: No available memory for the cache blocks. Try increasing gpu_memory_utilization...`, `Available KV cache memory: -1.95 GiB`) and the engine failed to start. Raised to 0.85 (matching p0_rollouts.py's working value) and it ran clean; full traceback was in avrl/runs/E04/judge.log before the fix, now overwritten by the successful run's log.

| quantity | E01 (majority-vote proxy) | E04 (judge proxy) |
|---|---|---|
| proxy/judge error rate | 14.5% | 14.4% |
| confident-subset error rate (share >= 0.75, n = 1,551) | 1.1% | 1.1% |
| AUC cheap / cheap+emb / emb-only | 0.923 / 0.922 / 0.606 | 0.922 / 0.921 / 0.606 |
| AUC cheap+emb minus cheap | -0.0007 (from E01's own numbers) | -0.0006 |
| neighbor ratio (cell30/100/300) | 1.00 / 1.03 / 1.04 | 1.00 / 1.04 / 1.04 |
| Jaccard(majority-wrong, judge-wrong) | n/a | 0.993 (433 intersection / 436 union) |
| judge_pick == majority answer | n/a | 99.27% of groups (2,978/3,000) |

Root cause, checked directly (not just trusting the aggregate number): judge_pick equals the majority answer in 2,978 of 3,000 groups (99.27%). Cross-tab of judge_error against majority's own proxy_error shows all 433 judge errors are also majority errors, judge is correct on 3 of majority's 436 errors, and wrong on zero cases majority got right. This is a mechanism artifact, not evidence that the judge is a good verifier: the tally rule (yes-vote weight = self-consistency count if judge says "yes", tie broken by that same count) means that whenever the judge says "yes" to the majority answer, which the log shows it does in the overwhelming majority of cases, the majority answer wins regardless of what it says about other candidates. Of the 22 groups where judge_pick differed from the majority answer, 19 of those were cases where the majority's own extracted answer was "0" (an extraction-failure placeholder, not a real majority), so the judge's "independent" signal barely surfaced anywhere in this run.

1. "Of the 22 groups where judge_pick differed from the majority answer, 19 of those were cases where the majority's own extracted answer was '0'" is incorrect. Recomputing directly from judge_scores.parquet merged with groups.parquet: of the 22 differing groups, 17 have majority == "0" and the remaining 5 have majority == "" (empty string, a second extraction-failure form, not "0"). Neither 19 nor "all were '0'" is right; the correct split is 17 literal "0" plus 5 empty-string. This does not change the paragraph's conclusion (all 22 are extraction-failure placeholders, not real majority answers, so the judge's independent signal still barely surfaces), but the specific count and the "were '0'" characterization should read "17 of 22 ... (the remaining 5 have an empty-string extracted answer, also a failure case, not '0')".
2. The table's "AUC cheap+emb minus cheap ... -0.0007 (from E01's own numbers)" does not match runs/p0/result.json: auc_cheap_emb (0.9223188862768769) minus auc_cheap (0.9230886365179956) = -0.00076975, which rounds to -0.0008 at 4 decimal places, not -0.0007.

Everything else checked out: judge_error_rate, confident-subset n and rate, auc_cheap/auc_cheap_emb/auc_emb_only for E04, neighbor ratios, Jaccard (433/436 = 0.9931), judge_pick==majority (2,978/3,000 = 99.27%), the judge_error/proxy_error cross-tab (433 both-wrong, 3 judge-correct-majority-wrong, 0 judge-wrong-majority-correct), the 24,000-rollouts-to-10,168-unique-pairs dedup count, and judge_all_no_frac = 0.0. No gold leakage into the judge prompt or into the AUC feature sets (cheap + pc0-15 only). No budget/policy accounting applies (no new generation, pure proxy diagnostic on existing rollouts). judge.log shows a benign post-shutdown "EngineCore died unexpectedly" line after "Shutdown complete" and after the summary JSON was already printed and written to disk; this is vLLM client/server IPC cleanup noise, not a truncation or a hidden failure, and result.json/analyze.log are internally consistent with judge.log's own summary. Sample size (433 judge_error=1 groups, n=3,000 total) is well above the <10 kill floor, and the pre-registered pass/kill thresholds in the entry match both the task spec and exp/e04_structure.py's pass_/kill logic verbatim.

Corrected verdict: unchanged, still KILL. Jaccard = 0.993 > 0.8 and auc_cheap_emb - auc_cheap = -0.0006 for E04 (confirmed) are decisive on their own regardless of the two narrative-number errors above; neither correction moves any number across the pass/kill thresholds. The entry's qualitative conclusion (proxy-type variation unsupported by this run; tally-mechanism confound, not necessarily a real judge-vs-majority finding) also stands. Treat the "19 of 22 were '0'" and "-0.0007" figures as corrected to "17 of 22 were '0' (5 more were empty-string)" and "-0.0008" respectively before citing this entry elsewhere.

This is a mechanism artifact, not evidence that the judge is a good verifier: the tally rule (yes-vote weight = self-consistency count if judge says "yes", tie broken by that same count) means that whenever the judge says "yes" to the majority answer, which the log shows it does in the overwhelming majority of cases, the majority answer wins regardless of what it says about other candidates. E04's own pre-registered design (self-consistency-weighted tie-break) is the likely confound, not necessarily a real finding about judge-type proxies in general. Hypothesis: self-verification (the same policy, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, re-asked to independently re-derive and check each of its own stored answers without seeing its prior chain of thought) produces a proxy-error signal that is measurably distinct from the majority-vote proxy's (E01), rather than a redundant copy of it, giving a clean second point on the proxy-type-variation axis for claim 3 without E04's/L5a's self-consistency-tie-break confound.

Run: policy model Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (vLLM, temperature 1.0, top_p 1.0, max_tokens 512, seed=1, distinct from E01's rollout seed=0), question only, no gold and no prior chain of thought shown, same 3,000 GSM8K groups x 8 rollouts as E01/E04 (avrl/runs/p0/groups.parquet, rollouts.parquet, feats.parquet). New generation: 24,000 independent re-derivations. self_verify_error per group = 1 if this pass's majority answer differs from the group's original stored majority answer (mirrors proxy_error's majority != gold definition, but against the original majority rather than gold, so the two labels are directly comparable). Scripts: avrl/exp/e05_selfverify.py (generation), avrl/exp/e05_structure.py (comparison/structure), avrl/e05_chain.sh (chain). Files: avrl/runs/E05/selfverify.parquet, selfverify_summary.json, selfverify.log, structure.log, result.json. One claim in the entry does not hold up: "Sample size (3,000 groups, same population as E01/E04/L5a) is unchanged and well above any reasonable noise floor for the observed gap sizes." Verdict against this diagnostic's own pre-registered bar (>=10% relative improvement of combined_flag over agreement_only at 25% budget = support a separate arm; otherwise no support): NO_SUPPORT. agreement_only dominates both alternative signals at every budget tested. sv_agreement_only underperforms agreement_only at all three budgets (191.0 vs 223.5 at 10%; 331.9 vs 358.8 at 25%; 413.5 vs 419.8 at 50%) despite E05's finding that self-verification's error SET only partially overlaps majority-vote's -- the partial-overlap signal does not translate into a better ranking, it is simply a noisier one. combined_flag is far worse than agreement_only at low and medium budgets (89.8 vs 223.5 at 10%; 224.5 vs 358.8 at 25%) because it discards agreement's continuous ranking information for a coarse binary gate covering nearly half the dataset at only 28.9% precision; it only catches up to agreement_only at 50% budget (421.3 vs 419.8, within noise) once the budget is large enough that precision stops mattering as much.

| neighbor ratio cell100 (confident subset) | 1.16x | 0.46x |

One wrinkle not covered by the pre-registered metrics: within the confident subset only (n=726), AUC actually rose with embeddings (cheap 0.588, cheap+emb 0.648, gain +0.060), the opposite sign from the full-population gap. This does not change the verdict below (the pre-registered AUC metric is defined on the full population, matching how E01's own -0.0008 baseline is computed; the neighbor-ratio metric already kills decisively on its own), but at n=726 a positive AUC swing this size inside one subset is plausibly a small-sample artifact rather than real structure, and is flagged here rather than silently dropped.

Verdict against the pre-registered thresholds: KILL. Pass required all three: confident-subset proxy_error_rate >= 3.1pp above E01 (needs >= 3.1%), AND auc_cheap_emb - auc_cheap >= 0.05, AND neighbor_ratio(cell100) >= 1.5. Observed: confident-subset rate 4.27% clears its bar (+3.17pp), but auc_cheap_emb - auc_cheap is -0.0032 (fails, wrong sign) and neighbor_ratio(cell100) is 0.46x (fails, and below 1.0, meaning a wrong answer's embedding neighbors in the confident subset are less likely than chance to also be wrong at this smaller model). What it changes: extends the threshold-regime kill (E01, E04/L5a, E05, all at 1.5B) to a second, weaker model (0.5B). The large-model end of this axis (something bigger than 1.5B) remains untested and is the only part of "model size" not yet ruled out.

Run: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, MBPP (HF google-research-datasets/mbpp, config full, train+test+validation deduped to 964 rows, 600 sampled with seed 0), 8 rollouts per problem (vLLM, temperature 1.0, top_p 1.0, max_tokens 512). Prompt showed the problem text plus the first test's assert (standard MBPP practice, implies the function name). Cheap proxy = majority vote over each program's output-signature: run the program on the test inputs only (never the expected outputs), record the tuple of outputs/exception types across the problem's test_list, vote on the modal tuple. Verdict against the pre-registered rule (pass if auc_cheap_emb-auc_cheap>=0.05 or neighbor_ratio_cell100>=1.5; kill if both fail; inconclusive if fewer than 60 proxy-error groups): KILL. What it changes: Even with no discrete self-consistency signal available at all, proxy error (reward-model top-pick not gold-positive) still does not cluster in prompt-embedding space beyond what cheap scalar features (RM score stats, length, consistency) already capture. This is the third kill (E01, E08, E09) across three structurally different proxy mechanisms (majority vote over answers, majority vote over output signatures, reward-model score), which narrows claim 3's remaining room: no proxy mechanism tried so far gives embeddings anything to add.

Verdict against the pre-registered rule, applied to the primary config (cell100, cheap, matches E01/E03/L3a/L4a/E08's standard reporting config): PASS. greedy_online vs static_matched at 25% budget: point diff +12.5 hits (111.1 vs 98.6), relative improvement +12.7%, 95% CI on the relative improvement [+3.9%, +25.5%], excluding zero on the positive side. This is the first config in the whole project (E01, E03, L3a, L4a, E08, P1-goldberg-s0/s1) where the learned allocator significantly beats a fair, budget-matched threshold.

What it changes: this is the first point where the cheap signal is weak enough (cheap AUC 0.73, vs 0.83-0.91 on E01/E08, and the AUC gap/neighbor-ratio structure test above still killed claim 3) that the learned allocator earns a real, bootstrap-significant edge over static_matched, exactly the regime the project's structure-statistic-versus-gain curve predicted claim 2 would need. The result generalizes qualitatively across both group_col groupings and both feature sets at 25% and 50% budget (greedy_online vs static_matched excludes zero on the positive side in 7 of 8 of those cells; the one exception, cell100/cheap_pc/25% for ts_online, still trends positive) but not at 10% budget, where every CI in the table includes zero -- the edge needs enough budget to let the online classifier refit before it beats a threshold fit once on a free-labeled quarter. ts_online is weaker and less consistent than greedy_online (fails to exclude zero at cell100/cheap_pc/25% and cell30/cheap_pc/50%): the plain self-trained ranking without Thompson layout over buckets, not the bucket-level exploration logic, is carrying this result. Caveat that keeps this from being an unqualified win for claim 2: greedy_online never significantly beats "static" (the free-label analog) at any budget or config tested here -- every greedy_online-vs-static CI in the table includes zero, and the point estimate favors static at 10% budget in 3 of 4 configs. So the learned allocator closes most but not all of the gap to a threshold that gets free labels beyond its budget; it does not yet surpass that stronger, budget-unmatched baseline. Given E09's own caveats (fallback 3B judge, 30% of proxy-error groups structurally unwinnable, 18% prompt contamination, all noted in the entry above and not reverified here), this PASS should be read as a real but noisier signal than E01/E08's clean kills, not a final word on claim 2.

Follow-ups:
1. The in-training rerun on this task (harness v2, following P1-goldberg-s0/s1's pattern but swapped onto HelpSteer2/RM-proxy/judge-gold instead of GSM8K) is the test that actually matters for claim 2: this entry and P1-goldberg-s0/s1 together show the replay and the in-training result agreeing exactly on GSM8K (both kill), so the replay's first PASS here needs the same in-training check before it changes any funding decision.
2. A second open-ended dataset (different prompt distribution and/or a different cheap-vs-expensive proxy pair, e.g. a weaker RM or a different judge-capability gap) would test whether "weak cheap signal" is the right generalizable condition for claim 2 to hold, or whether this PASS is specific to E09's particular proxy pair and its noted gold-label issues.

Follow-ups:
1. If kill or inconclusive: the remaining untried axis for claim 3 is a stronger/weaker judge-proxy capability gap (e.g. a 1.5B proxy against this same 7B judge, or this reward model against a weaker judge) or a multi-step agentic task, rather than another single-turn task.
2. Judge parse failures under max_tokens=8 are an honest data-quality cost of this design; a targeted retry with more tokens on unparseable rows would tighten the gold labels if this point is extended or reused.
3. judge_model_used=Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct (fallback_used=True): if the 7B judge had to fall back to the 3B, the judge itself is weaker than planned and the gold labels should be treated as noisier than E01/E08's gold (exact answer / test execution).
4. The allocation replay (sim_*.json under avrl/runs/E09b/) should be folded into the claim-2 budget curve (L3a/L4a) alongside E01 and E08, same as E08's entry proposed.

| confident subset (def. differs: agreement>=0.75 for E01/E08, top-quartile rm_gap12 for E09), n: error rate / cheap AUC / cheap+emb AUC / neighbor ratio | 1.1% / 0.63 / 0.53 / 1.16 (n=1,551) | 20.2% / 0.73 / 0.72 / 1.45 (n=243) | 5.1% / 0.74 / 0.79 / 2.02 (n=1,000) |

The confident-subset neighbor ratio of 2.02, which PROJECT.md calls "the first clear prompt-space structure in the project," gets closer scrutiny here since it is the strongest positive-sounding number this project has produced and is not itself part of the pre-registered pass/kill rule (that rule only checks the full-dataset neighbor_ratio_cell100=1.14, which fails). Recomputed directly from feats.parquet: the 1,000-group confident subset (top-quartile rm_gap12) carries 51 proxy-error groups spread across 31 of its 100 cell100 cells (never more than 5 errors in one cell, cell 64 with 19 members), reproducing D.neighbor_hit_ratio's 2.024408583492394 exactly. A permutation null (reshuffling the 51 error labels within the subset 1,000 times, cell100 membership fixed) gives mean 0.99, 95th percentile 1.386, max over 1,000 draws 1.735; 0 of 1,000 permutations reached or exceeded the observed 2.024 (empirical p<0.001). Leave-one-cell-out, dropping each of the 31 error-carrying cells one at a time, moves the ratio only between 1.994 (dropping cell 64, its single largest contributor) and 2.144 (dropping a 1-error cell); no single cell is carrying the result. So 2.02 is not a fluke of multiple testing or one hot cluster, and it is corroborated by an independent prior run: E09c (same 7B/AWQ judge, a different prompt sample via E09b's rollouts) already measured a confident-subset neighbor ratio of 1.84, while both 3B-fallback-judge runs (E09, E09b) measured 0.94 and 0.70 (no clustering at all). That is a real, judge-identity-correlated, twice-replicated pattern, not a one-off E09d artifact, and PROJECT.md's table and prose should say so instead of presenting 2.02 as unprecedented; as written it omits that E09c already cleared 1.5x on the same statistic.

That said, three things keep this from being a clean positive result. (1) Absolute power is thin: 51 events is below the project's own 60-event reliability floor used elsewhere for n_proxy_error_groups, even though the permutation test is sound at this n. (2) A hand-check of 10 random proxy-error groups (prompt, top-RM response, its judge score, the group's best-judged response) found: 1/10 (pid 256) is an "unwinnable" group where all 8 rollouts scored gold-negative, so proxy_error=1 regardless of proxy quality; unwinnable groups are 43/4,000 overall (1.1%) but 43/290 (14.8%) of all errors and 9/51 (17.6%) of confident-subset errors, so they are over-represented among errors. Quantifying the rest of the sample: the RM's top pick is a refusal-like response ("I'm sorry, I can't...") in only 5.75% of all groups (230/4,000), but those groups have a 22.2% proxy-error rate versus 6.3% elsewhere (3.5x), a real and mechanistically sensible failure mode (the RM penalizes refusals on average, mean rm_score -1.97 vs -0.28, but not always enough within a given group of 8 to keep them off the top). This accounts for 51/290 (17.6%) of all errors but only 7/51 (13.7%) of confident-subset errors, and a neighbor-ratio check on "RM top pick is a refusal" as its own label gives only 1.40 in the confident subset (lower than proxy_error's 2.02, and concentrated in only 5 of the 31 error-carrying cells), so refusal-clustering is a real contributor but does not fully explain the structure; 35/51 (68.6%) confident-subset errors are neither unwinnable nor refusal-driven, and the remaining hand-checked examples (pid 3520, 2197, 1185, 2641) look more like judge threshold noise (several groups have gold scores bunched at 4-7, straddling the >=7 cutoff) or the judge's inability to fact-check a confidently-worded hallucination than a clean quality gap. Net: proxy_error carries real signal, not pure judge noise, but it is a mix of at least three distinct mechanisms (unwinnable groups, a specific RM refusal-bias, and judge-threshold/fact-check noise), not a single clean construct. (3) Judge health is improved over E09's 3B fallback but not clean: of 32,000 scores, 29.1% are 7 and 48.3% are 8 (77.4% combined), while 9 is a round-number "valley" at only 1.6% (vs 4.1% for 10), the same coarse-rounding bias flagged before, now at the real 7B/AWQ judge rather than only the fallback. More importantly, this judge rewards truncation: mean gold_score 7.21 for truncated rollouts (37.2% of all 32,000) versus 6.92 for complete ones, and gold-positive rate 87.4% truncated versus 80.5% complete, while the RM scores truncation the opposite way (mean rm_score -0.75 truncated vs -0.21 complete). The original E09 critic note attributed this length/verbosity bias to being "specific to the fallback judge"; E09d shows the same qualitative bias with the real 7B judge running in eager mode, so that attribution was wrong and should be corrected: the bias is a property of this scoring setup (max_tokens=8 rubric, max_tokens=384 generation) in general, not the fallback model specifically.

The sim replay numbers are confirmed exactly: avrl/runs/E09d/sim_cell100_cheap.json budget_0.25 gives static=126.0, static_matched=102.625, greedy_online=121.875, ts_online=134.25, uniform=54.25, oracle=225.0, matching PROJECT.md's rounded 126.0/102.6/121.9/134.2/54.2/225 to the displayed decimal. What ts_online can exploit that greedy_online cannot: ts_online keeps a Beta posterior per cell100 cluster (reinforced online by a classifier-derived per-cell prior) and Thompson-samples which cell to visit next, so it can concentrate budget on whole clusters with a higher empirical hit rate even for member groups whose own cheap features look unremarkable; greedy_online has no notion of cluster at all and only re-ranks individual unseen groups by a single global self-trained classifier score, so it can only exploit per-group cheap-feature signal, never the between-cell variance the neighbor-ratio statistic measures. However, PROJECT.md's claim that E09d is "the first point where the bandit over prompt cells beats the greedy self-trainer" is stated as a finding in running prose while the same sentence admits "Bootstrap pending (L9d)": this rests on a single fit/sim split with 8 policy seeds, not the 300-group-resample bootstrap that L9a/L9b/L9c required before trusting any greedy-vs-ts_online comparison on this task family, and L9a's own bootstrapped result on E09 found the opposite ranking ("ts_online is weaker and less consistent than greedy_online... the plain self-trained ranking without Thompson layout over buckets, not the bucket-level exploration logic, is carrying this result"). Until L9d exists, this specific claim should be treated as an unconfirmed point estimate, not a project milestone, the same caution L9c applied to E09c's thinner point.

That said, three things keep this from being a clean positive result. (1) Absolute power is thin: 51 events is below the project's own 60-event reliability floor used elsewhere for n_proxy_error_groups, even though the permutation test is sound at this n. (2) A hand-check of 10 random proxy-error groups (prompt, top-RM response, its judge score, the group's best-judged response) found: 1/10 (pid 256) is an "unwinnable" group where all 8 rollouts scored gold-negative, so proxy_error=1 regardless of proxy quality; unwinnable groups are 43/4,000 overall (1.1%) but 43/290 (14.8%) of all errors and 9/51 (17.6%) of confident-subset errors, so they are over-represented among errors. Quantifying the rest of the sample: the RM's top pick is a refusal-like response ("I'm sorry, I can't...") in only 5.75% of all groups (230/4,000), but those groups have a 22.2% proxy-error rate versus 6.3% elsewhere (3.5x), a real and mechanistically sensible failure mode (the RM penalizes refusals on average, mean rm_score -1.97 vs -0.28, but not always enough within a given group of 8 to keep them off the top). This accounts for 51/290 (17.6%) of all errors but only 7/51 (13.7%) of confident-subset errors, and a neighbor-ratio check on "RM top pick is a refusal" as its own label gives only 1.40 in the confident subset (lower than proxy_error's 2.02, and concentrated in only 5 of the 31 error-carrying cells), so refusal-clustering is a real contributor but does not fully explain the structure; 35/51 (68.6%) confident-subset errors are neither unwinnable nor refusal-driven, and the remaining hand-checked examples (pid 3520, 2197, 1185, 2641) look more like judge threshold noise (several groups have gold scores bunched at 4-7, straddling the >=7 cutoff) or the judge's inability to fact-check a confidently-worded hallucination than a clean quality gap. Net: proxy_error carries real signal, not pure judge noise, but it is a mix of at least three distinct mechanisms (unwinnable groups, a specific RM refusal-bias, and judge-threshold/fact-check noise), not a single clean construct. (3) Judge health is improved over E09's 3B fallback but not clean: of 32,000 scores, 29.1% are 7 and 48.3% are 8 (77.4% combined), while 9 is a round-number "valley" at only 1.6% (vs 4.1% for 10), the same coarse-rounding bias flagged before, now at the real 7B/AWQ judge rather than only the fallback. More importantly, this judge rewards truncation: mean gold_score 7.21 for truncated rollouts (37.2% of all 32,000) versus 6.92 for complete ones, and gold-positive rate 87.4% truncated versus 80.5% complete, while the RM scores truncation the opposite way (mean rm_score -0.75 truncated vs -0.21 complete). The original E09 critic note attributed this length/verbosity bias to being "specific to the fallback judge"; E09d shows the same qualitative bias with the real 7B judge running in eager mode, so that attribution was wrong and should be corrected: the bias is a property of this scoring setup (max_tokens=8 rubric, max_tokens=384 generation) in general, not the fallback model specifically.

The sim replay numbers are confirmed exactly: avrl/runs/E09d/sim_cell100_cheap.json budget_0.25 gives static=126.0, static_matched=102.625, greedy_online=121.875, ts_online=134.25, uniform=54.25, oracle=225.0, matching PROJECT.md's rounded 126.0/102.6/121.9/134.2/54.2/225 to the displayed decimal. What ts_online can exploit that greedy_online cannot: ts_online keeps a Beta posterior per cell100 cluster (reinforced online by a classifier-derived per-cell prior) and Thompson-samples which cell to visit next, so it can concentrate budget on whole clusters with a higher empirical hit rate even for member groups whose own cheap features look unremarkable; greedy_online has no notion of cluster at all and only re-ranks individual unseen groups by a single global self-trained classifier score, so it can only exploit per-group cheap-feature signal, never the between-cell variance the neighbor-ratio statistic measures. However, PROJECT.md's claim that E09d is "the first point where the bandit over prompt cells beats the greedy self-trainer" is stated as a finding in running prose while the same sentence admits "Bootstrap pending (L9d)": this rests on a single fit/sim split with 8 policy seeds, not the 300-group-resample bootstrap that L9a/L9b/L9c required before trusting any greedy-vs-ts_online comparison on this task family, and L9a's own bootstrapped result on E09 found the opposite ranking ("ts_online is weaker and less consistent than greedy_online... the plain self-trained ranking without Thompson layout over buckets, not the bucket-level exploration logic, is carrying this result"). Until L9d exists, this specific claim should be treated as an unconfirmed point estimate, not a project milestone, the same caution L9c applied to E09c's thinner point.

Verdict: the KILL label and every number in the E09d ledger entry are correct and reproducible; this is the most carefully executed point in the E09 family (real 7B/AWQ judge confirmed with no fallback, eager mode fixing the prior OOM, 4x the prompts, markup stripped) and its primary pre-registered result should be trusted as-is. The confident-subset neighbor ratio of 2.02 is a real, permutation-significant (p<0.001), non-single-cell-driven, twice-replicated-under-the-7B-judge effect, so it is more than noise. But PROJECT.md overstates it on two counts: it is presented as unprecedented when E09c already cleared the same bar (1.84), and the "bandit beats greedy self-trainer" framing is asserted ahead of the bootstrap confirmation this project's own methodology requires for that specific comparison, with a prior bootstrap (L9a) having found the opposite direction. E09d can bear real weight for "proxy error is not pure noise and has some exploitable concentration in a reward-model-proxy/strong-judge regime," but it cannot yet bear the weight of "claim 3 has a confirmed win" or "the bandit allocator is confirmed better than greedy" until L9d's bootstrap lands; both should be downgraded to provisional until then.

The cell bandit's point estimates exceed the greedy self-trainer's at every budget but the intervals overlap, so the bandit-versus-greedy ordering remains provisional. TIE on both points / inconclusive stands as the correct result under the pre-registered CI-sign rule; nothing about the core E09/E09d head-to-head numbers, the script diff, or the budget/leakage accounting needs correction. The one fix is to follow-up 2's runtime estimate: replace "roughly 10-11 min of CPU time each based on E09/E09d's observed runtimes" with an estimate consistent with this entry's own data, e.g. roughly 3-5 min each if goldberg's load matches this run, though the original L12b sweep for these same points ran 4-5x slower under then-current contention, so budgeting up to about 10 min to be safe is still reasonable, just not for the stated reason.

Verdict: pass (pre-registered M08 rule: greedy admits at least 15 percent fewer corrupted groups than the threshold in both seeds; observed 25 and 33 percent fewer). Quality: tie in seed 0, +0.13 in seed 1, inside noise. The bandit-flavoured arm ties the threshold; the layout-free self-trainer beats it, and its admissions fall over training (10, 8, 6, 6 and 5, 10, 4, 7) while the threshold's do not, the opposite of the GSM8K picture.
What it changes: first in-training support for claim 2, and the first in-training point that separates the two regimes with the right baseline. On GSM8K the label-free confidence signal (vote agreement) is strong and the threshold wins (M07: 26 vs 35); on the open-ended task the label-free signal (reward-model gap) is weak and the self-trainer wins. The predictive statistic is the AUC of the label-free confidence feature alone, measured on a pre-training probe. Pending: M08 (same comparison with the 4-bit 7B judge at 150 steps on goldberg), M07 and M06 second seeds, hannah four-arm runs.
Confidence-feature AUCs for proxy error (label-free, single feature, measured on the phase-0 samples): GSM8K vote agreement 0.914 (1.5B, E01) and 0.874 (0.5B, E06); open-ended reward-model top-two gap 0.509 (E09b) and 0.569 (E09d), barely above chance, while the free-text consistency analogue (mean pairwise MiniLM cosine among the 8 responses) reaches 0.69. So the in-training open-ended "threshold" arm is close to a random allocator, which is why the self-trainer beats it, and a stronger label-free rule for free text should rank by consistency (M09).

What it changes: the in-training picture is now uniform. In every setting tested (GSM8K at 1.5B and 0.5B, MBPP in replay, open-ended with a reward-model proxy), a label-free threshold on the cheap grader's own consistency signal (vote agreement for exact answers, response consistency for free text) is the best verification allocator at equal budget; the learned allocators lose or tie, and the cell bandit is always worst. The thesis claim becomes: self-consistency gating is a near-optimal, label-free rule for budgeted verification in RL post-training; learned allocation does not improve on it; and the diagnostic that predicts this is the AUC of the consistency signal measured on a pre-training probe. Seed 1's proxy error is flat (0.059 first quarter, 0.054 last) where seed 0's fell from 0.117 to 0.045, so the "shrinking error" pattern is itself seed-dependent.
What it changes: with the 7B judge the open-ended task sits in the regime where allocation does not matter: base corruption is 6 to 7 percent of groups and no rule, fixed or learned, moves it. The M09 result (3B judge, 18 percent base error) stays the only setting where the consistency threshold clearly wins, and M07/M06 (exact-answer tasks) the settings where the agreement threshold clearly wins. Revised statement for the thesis: a confidence-ranked threshold is never beaten by a learned allocator at equal budget in any of the six in-training settings, and its advantage over random allocation scales with the cheap grader's base error rate and the confidence AUC (large on GSM8K and the 3B-judge task, nil here). The regime diagnostic predicts which case a user is in before training; the honest product is the diagnostic plus the threshold recipe, not a learned router.

Verdict: KILL for the question as posed (base model plus signature-vote grader). No arm beats the base model; the proxy arm collapses to 0.5 percent, the two budgeted arms land between proxy and full, and even the fully verified arm drifts slightly below base (0.065 vs 0.088, eval SE about 2 points) because the reward is too sparse (1.2 percent pass rate, E10p0). This is the first setting where corrupted rewards visibly destroy quality: when the cheap grader is wrong on 99 percent of groups, every unverified group pushes the policy toward the most common wrong program. Together with M10 (GSM8K, 4 to 10 percent corruption, no accuracy effect) it brackets the thesis's primary metric: corrupted-reward counts matter in proportion to the cheap grader's error rate, and the step-0 diagnostic (99 percent here) would have predicted the collapse before training. The fix is E10b (Instruct start, visible-test grader, curriculum), whose proxy arm on goldberg is already at 0.22 held-out pass@1 against 0.145 reference; hannah four-arm seed 0 is job 78892, queued behind 78891.

Verdict: with the judge reward shaped like the proxy reward (top half of each group), verifying every group lands at the quarter-budget consistency threshold's level on both seeds (4.685 vs 4.68, 4.655 vs 4.565; both within the 0.15 bar), and the seed-0 full-absolute score of 4.92 is the only point above that band. So the held-out advantage of full verification seen in M11 came from the absolute reward shape (a response is rewarded only if the judge scores it 7 or more, which lets the group's reward reflect absolute quality), not from the labels the budgeted arms lacked. Claim 1 therefore PASSES on the open-ended task like for like: at equal reward shape, the consistency threshold at a quarter of the judge calls matches full judging. Two follow-ups worth one line each: (1) a quarter-budget arm whose verified groups use the absolute reward would test whether a small number of absolute-reward groups recovers the 4.92 (cheap to run, not yet queued); (2) the absolute-vs-rank reward shape is itself a design choice a framework user should know about, since it moved held-out quality more than any allocation rule did.

Verdict: calls and quality PASS, corruption target FAIL (7.5 percent against 4). Cause, in two parts: the harness verifies round(budget x 8) groups per step, so 0.15 became 0.125 and the burn-in grid's value for 0.125 lies between its 0.10 (8 percent) and 0.15 (4 percent) points; and the burn-in estimate from 200 groups has a wide interval (threshold at 0.25 was 0.040 with interval 0.015 to 0.060). Product fix pre-registered as PRODUCT-4: recommend only realizable budgets (multiples of 1/groups per step), round up, and meet the target with the upper confidence bound of the curve rather than the point estimate; on these rows that would choose 0.25 or 0.375, in line with the fixed-budget threshold arms (4 percent at 0.25). The loop itself behaved as designed; the picking rule was too optimistic.

Verdict: the pooled ratio meets the bar (0.878 below 0.9) but the count does not (seven of nine, not eight), so by the pre-registered rule claim 2 remains a TIE in the low-error regime. Reported alongside it, because the thesis should state what was seen: the self-trainer admits about twelve percent fewer wrong rewards than the label-free rule in this regime, with a pooled z near 1.9 (two-sided p about 0.06), consistently in sign on seven of nine seeds, and never in the strong-signal settings (M06, M07) where it loses clearly. Held-out quality is tied in every one of the nine comparisons (M15 seed 3: 7.76 greedy against 7.785 threshold under the 4-bit judge with the fixed evaluation). The honest sentence for the thesis: a learned allocator can shave a further ten percent off the wrong-reward count when the cheap grader's confidence signal is weak (AUC about 0.68), at the cost of a learned component, and buys nothing when the signal is strong; the label-free threshold remains the recommended default.
